reviews.title: Nguyễn Trung Sơn · IELTS 48 · W09 · Đề 1
reviews.scopeMarkdown:
**Số từ bài gốc: 190 từ**, đếm trên nguyên văn bằng cách tách theo khoảng trắng; đạt yêu cầu 150–200 từ.
Phạm vi: Cô chấm Đề 1 đã gõ; chưa chấm Đề 2 hoặc bản scan.
reviews.overall: Em cần sửa và nộp lại. Bài này em làm còn ẩu ở phần xác định đại lượng. Mở bài dùng “how many” nên chuyển tỷ lệ phần trăm thành số nữ nghị sĩ; Detail 2 tiếp tục sai đại lượng ở “the UK started” và “France fluctuated”. Overview còn thiếu nước có tỷ lệ phần trăm thấp nhất. Em đã dùng các cấu trúc được học như “with the UK experiencing”, “with a subsequent steady growth” và “after which”, nhưng vẫn cần kiểm tra chủ thể và quy chiếu. Mục đích của việc ghi chép là hiểu và vận dụng để tự viết. Cô yêu cầu em tự sửa những chỗ đánh dấu trước khi nộp lại.
reviews.dataGrouping: Detail 1 trình bày Italy rồi Germany; đây là hai nước có tỷ lệ phần trăm cao nhất vào cuối kỳ. Detail 2 trình bày United Kingdom, Belgium rồi France và nối bằng đặc điểm “lower starting figures”: cả ba đều bắt đầu thấp hơn hai nước ở Detail 1. Cô giữ nguyên nhóm và thứ tự này; France có thể ở nhóm ấy vì em đang so sánh mức đầu kỳ, Cô cũng làm rõ vị trí dẫn đầu của France năm 2004. Các mốc cần bổ sung được chữa ở C05.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given line chart illustrates how many female members of parliament there were in five European countries from 2000 to 2012.
     Overall, there was a general increase in the proportion of female parliamentarians across all five nations, with the UK experiencing the most pronounced rise. Also of note is that Germany consistently had the highest figures for most of the period, before being overtaken by Italy at the end.
     To elaborate, starting at nearly 27% in 2000, the percentage of female parliamentarians in Italy rose to about 31% in 2004, with a subsequent steady growth and a final figure of nearly 39% in 2012. The figures for Germany began at roughly 33% in 2000, after which it climbed gradually to end the period at nearly 37%.
     Regarding categories with lower starting figures, the UK started at around 4% in 2000, after which it experienced a rise to nearly 20% in 2008 before ending the period at roughly 28% in 2012. A similar upward pattern was recorded in the figures for Belgium, going from 17% to 28%, while France fluctuated, peaking at around 37% in 2004 before finishing at roughly 32%.
originalParagraphs: The given line chart illustrates how many female members of parliament there were in five European countries from 2000 to 2012.

Overall, there was a general increase in the proportion of female parliamentarians across all five nations, with the UK experiencing the most pronounced rise. Also of note is that Germany consistently had the highest figures for most of the period, before being overtaken by Italy at the end.

To elaborate, starting at nearly 27% in 2000, the percentage of female parliamentarians in Italy rose to about 31% in 2004, with a subsequent steady growth and a final figure of nearly 39% in 2012. The figures for Germany began at roughly 33% in 2000, after which it climbed gradually to end the period at nearly 37%.

Regarding categories with lower starting figures, the UK started at around 4% in 2000, after which it experienced a rise to nearly 20% in 2008 before ending the period at roughly 28% in 2012. A similar upward pattern was recorded in the figures for Belgium, going from 17% to 28%, while France fluctuated, peaking at around 37% in 2004 before finishing at roughly 32%.

Vị trí: câu Introduction. Em viết “how many female members of parliament there were” → sửa thành “how female representation in parliament, expressed as a percentage, changed”. How many hỏi có bao nhiêu người, trong khi biểu đồ đo tỷ lệ phần trăm nữ nghị sĩ trong nghị viện của từng nước. **Loại: Lỗi cần sửa. Ưu tiên: Bắt buộc sửa.**

annotations.headerMarkdown: **C05 · Detail 2: chọn đủ mốc và diễn biến nổi bật**

Vị trí: câu 2 Detail 2. Em viết Belgium “going from 17% to 28%” và France “peaking at around 37% in 2004 before finishing at roughly 32%”.

Với Belgium, em bổ sung mốc đạt khoảng 28% vào năm 2004, sau đó gần như ổn định: “The figure for Belgium increased from 17% to 28% by 2004, after which it remained relatively stable.” Hai mức đầu–cuối hiện tại chưa cho thấy diễn biến này.

Với France, em đã chọn đúng đỉnh nhưng thiếu mức đầu kỳ. Em bổ sung khoảng 25% năm 2000, giữ đỉnh 37% năm 2004 và mức cuối khoảng 31% năm 2012, kèm diễn biến giảm rồi phục hồi sau đỉnh. Ba mốc này cho thấy tỷ lệ phần trăm tăng đầu–cuối dù kết thúc dưới đỉnh.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The given line chart illustrates how female representation in parliament, expressed as a percentage, changed in five European countries between 2000 and 2012.

Overall, the proportion of female parliamentarians increased in all five nations, most sharply in the United Kingdom. Germany generally had the highest figures, but Italy finished first, while the United Kingdom remained lowest, matching Belgium at the end.

To elaborate, in 2000, around 26% of parliamentarians in Italy were women, with a subsequent rise to 31% in 2004 and further growth to 39% in 2012. The figure for Germany also grew, from 33% to 37%, although its increase was smaller.

Regarding countries with lower starting figures, the proportion of female parliamentarians in the United Kingdom rose from about 3% in 2000 to 20% in 2008 and 28% in 2012. The figure for Belgium increased from 17% to 28% by 2004, after which it remained relatively stable. Meanwhile, that for France rose from 25% in 2000 to a peak of 37% in 2004, leading the chart, before falling and recovering to about 31% in 2012.

**Từ vựng và cấu trúc:** “with a subsequent rise to” dùng rise là danh từ, to chỉ mức đạt tới; were là động từ chính của câu. “after which it remained relatively stable” nối giai đoạn ổn định của Belgium sau năm 2004.

**Liên kết và đặc điểm chính:** “also grew … although its increase was smaller” nối điểm cùng tăng và mức tăng khác nhau của Italy–Germany. “matching Belgium at the end” làm rõ đồng hạng ở Overview; “leading the chart” chỉ vị trí của France tại đỉnh năm 2004.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given pie charts illustrate the main reasons why students chose a particular university in the UK in 1997 and 2007.
     Overall, there was a general increase in the proportion of students selecting universities based on suitable degree courses and proximity to parental home, with proximity to parental home experiencing the most pronounced rise. Also of note is that suitable degree courses consistently had the highest figures throughout the years.
     To elaborate, starting at 35% in 1997, the percentage of students choosing a university due to suitable degree courses rose to a final figure of 37% in 2007. The figures for proximity to parental home began at 10% in 1997, after which it climbed significantly to reach more than double at 22% in 2007.
     Regarding categories with declining figures, good sports and social activities started at 19% in 1997, after which it experienced a sharp decline to 6% in 2007. A similar downward pattern was recorded in the figures for quality of resources, decreasing from 21% to 17%, whereas quality of teaching experienced a slight rise from 15% to 18%.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The given pie charts illustrate how students' reasons for choosing a particular university in the United Kingdom differed between 1997 and 2007.

Overall, the proportions of students prioritizing suitable courses, proximity to parental home and teaching quality rose, whereas those for the other reasons fell. Suitable courses remained the leading reason, the figure for proximity recorded the greatest increase, and sports and social activities ranked last in 2007.

To elaborate, in 1997, 35% of students chose the university because of suitable degree courses, with a subsequent slight rise to 37% in 2007. The figure for proximity to parental home also rose, yet more markedly, from 10% to 22% over the same period, more than doubling.

Regarding the remaining reasons, the proportion of students prioritizing good sports and social activities started at 19% in 1997, after which it fell sharply to 6% in 2007. This was the largest decrease. A similar downward pattern was recorded in the figure for quality of resources, from 21% to 17%, whereas that for quality of teaching rose slightly from 15% to 18%.

reviews.originalEssay:
The given table illustrates the percentages of the population aged 65 and above in major three countries in 1988 and 2000, along with predictions for 2030.
     Overall, there was a general increase in the proportion of elderly people across all three countries, with Canada experiencing the most pronounced rise. Also of note is that Germany consistently had the highest figures throughout the years.
     To elaborate, starting at 16.45% in 1988, the percentage of seniors in Canada rose to 20.65% in 2000, with a subsequent steady growth and a predicted final figure of 26.35% in 2030. The figures for Germany began at 20.35% in 1988, after which it climbed to 25.53% in 2000 before projected to reach a peak of 30.65% at the end of the period.
     Regarding categories with lower figures, the UK started at 14.25% in 1988, after which it experienced a slight rise to 14.80% in 2000 before ending the forecast period at 20.45% in 2030. A similar upward pattern was recorded in the figures for all three nations, reflecting an aging population over the given timeframe.

reviews.suggestedRevision:
The table illustrates how the percentages of people aged 65 and over in Canada, Germany and the UK changed in 1988 and 2000, with predictions for 2030.

Overall, the proportions of elderly people increased in all three countries and are expected to rise further by 2030. Germany records the highest figures at every point and is predicted to experience the largest overall increase, whereas the UK remains the lowest.

In 1988, Germany had the highest proportion, at 20.35%, followed by Canada at 16.45%. By 2000, the figures for these two countries had risen to 25.53% and 20.65% respectively. Germany is then projected to reach 30.65% in 2030, while the percentage for Canada is expected to grow to 26.35%.

The UK started with the smallest percentage, at 14.25% in 1988, and saw only a slight rise to 14.80% in 2000. Its figure is forecast to increase more noticeably afterwards, reaching 20.45% in 2030. Thus, although all three countries follow an upward trend, the UK has lower proportions throughout the period.
